name: voc-ux-curiosity
description: "Use curiosity and assumption questioning in UX discovery to turn unexplained behavior into bounded, falsifiable research questions rather than speculative product demand."
---

# Curiosity and Passion

## Procedure
1. Identify an unexplained UX observation within the authorized research decision. Record its source and context in approved product-owned storage.
2. Ask what is assumed, whose perspective is missing, and which alternative explanation would change the decision. Avoid leading questions and unsupported claims about motivations.
3. Rank research questions by decision relevance and information gaps, not novelty. ProductOwner retains product priority and scope authority.
4. Propose a bounded observation or experiment with consent, inputs, exit criteria, and disconfirming evidence. No curiosity-driven participant contact or private-data access is implied.
5. Record what changed in the hypothesis and what remains unknown. Stop or escalate when the inquiry exceeds scope or adds no decision-relevant learning.

## Completion Checks
Questions are falsifiable and bounded; observed findings remain distinct from speculation. This skill operationalizes inquiry, not an assertion that an agent has human passion or has conducted research.
